reason: Follow the bone-cell lineage first, as the chapter suggests, before assembling the mature bone.
expectation: The signals will guide some stem-cell descendants toward bone-forming cells, though the precise stage is unclear.

alternatives.reason: Mineralizing the collagen framework also advances the skeleton, but I want to establish the cell lineage first.

effect: The lineage now connects matrix-producing osteoblasts to embedded osteocytes; next I can assemble the mature bone.
reaction: The transition from matrix-producing to embedded cells is interesting, though mesenchymal precursor is unexplained.
reason: Mineralizing the collagen framework is the only offered combination and should advance the arm skeleton.
expectation: Calcium phosphate crystals will combine with the collagen framework to form mineralized bone, though living cells may still need to be added.

effect: The framework now has mineral as well as collagen, clarifying their different contributions to bone strength.
reaction: The contrast between toughness and compression resistance is useful.
reason: Adding the bone cells is the only offered combination and continues the mature-bone assembly.
expectation: The bone cells will be shown within the mineralized framework, perhaps as embedded osteocytes.

effect: The mature bone cutaway now shows embedded cells connected through tiny channels; adding vessels is the next available step.
reaction: The channels make the idea of living cells inside hard bone more concrete.
reason: Adding blood vessels is the only offered combination and should supply the living bone.
expectation: The bones will gain a blood-vessel network that supplies their cells, though the picture may not show the full route to each cell.

effect: The cutaway now connects blood vessels to embedded bone cells through nutrient movement in the channel network.
reaction: Keeping red cells inside the vessel makes the nutrient route clear.
reason: Adding cartilage is the only offered combination and should prepare the bone ends for the elbow joint.
expectation: Cartilage will cap the contacting bone ends, providing smooth joint surfaces.

effect: The cartilage now caps the facing elbow surfaces, showing how they can slide against one another.
reaction: The sliding inset makes the cartilage's role clear.
reason: Adding the synovial capsule is the only offered combination and should continue assembling the joint.
expectation: The capsule will surround the elbow joint, with fluid inside; its precise contribution may be explained next.

effect: The capsule encloses the joint, and its lining supplies fluid that helps the cartilage surfaces glide.
reaction: The explanation makes the capsule's role clearer.
reason: Adding ligaments is the only offered combination and should help support the elbow.
expectation: The ligaments will connect the bones across the joint and help stabilize it while allowing movement.

effect: The ligaments complete the supported elbow, with the planned cutaway showing bending and resistance to sideways movement. The chapter goal is complete.
reaction: The contrasting movement arrows make the ligaments’ stabilizing role clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding bone cells and vessels was most worthwhile: the planned cutaways connect living embedded cells to channels and a nutrient supply inside hard bone.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding cartilage was fairly predictable and offered little explanation beyond the planned sliding inset.

surprise.text: The lineage from matrix-producing osteoblasts to embedded osteocytes changed my picture of bone as a living material. The term mesenchymal precursor, however, was unexplained.

arbitrary.text: No action lacked a clear purpose, though after the initial choice the compatible combinations were effectively prescribed rather than discoveries.

continue.text: I would continue: the connections between bone’s living cells, material properties and joint function were interesting, even if the choices became linear.
